ip_top_stories.title: Taylor & Francis and DataSeer Extend Partnership Helping Authors to Follow Journal Data Requirements
ip_top_stories.summary: Taylor & Francis has extended its partnership with DataSeer to help authors comply with journal data-sharing requirements. The collaboration aims to streamline the process of meeting data availability standards in academic publishing.

ip_top_stories.title: Uproar After Labour Tries to Scupper AI Copyright Law as Campaigners Vow to Come Back Fighting
ip_top_stories.summary: The UK government faced significant backlash after Labour moved to block proposed AI copyright legislation, which would have required AI companies to disclose when they use copyrighted material for training. Campaigners, including creators and rights holders, have vowed to continue pushing for stronger protections.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic Code Crisis Creates Copyright Contradiction
ip_top_stories.summary: Anthropic faces a copyright contradiction after its AI coding assistant was found to reproduce portions of licensed code, raising questions about whether AI-generated outputs infringe on the original works used in training. The incident highlights ongoing tensions between AI development practices and copyright law.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Tools Produce Thousands of Commercial Books
ip_top_stories.summary: AI tools are being used to generate thousands of commercial books, raising significant concerns about copyright ownership, market saturation, and the impact on human authors. The trend is prompting debate about regulatory and legal frameworks for AI-generated content in publishing.

ip_top_stories.title: CJEU Delivers Pastiche-Style Judgment on … Pastiche
ip_top_stories.summary: The Court of Justice of the European Union has issued a significant ruling on the pastiche exception in copyright law, clarifying the scope of the exception and its application to creative works. The IPKat reports this as an important development for European copyright jurisprudence.

ip_further_links.title: Delhi HC Directs Time-Bound Decision on AI Generated Artwork Copyright Plea
ip_further_links.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed authorities to make a time-bound decision on a petition seeking copyright protection for AI-generated artwork, marking a significant moment in India's approach to AI and intellectual property.

ip_further_links.title: AI Makes Securing Copyright Protection for Software Code Tricky Guide
ip_further_links.summary: A new guide examines why AI-assisted software development complicates copyright protection for code, given uncertainty over authorship and ownership of AI-generated outputs.

ip_further_links.title: Who Owns AI Copyright When Machines Create Art?
ip_further_links.summary: An explainer examines the unresolved legal question of who holds copyright in works created by AI systems, surveying different jurisdictional approaches and ongoing debates.

ip_further_links.title: MPA Chief On 'Going To The Mat' With Instagram, Copyright, AI & Pushing A Federal Film Tax Incentive
ip_further_links.summary: The Motion Picture Association's chief executive discusses the organisation's aggressive stance on AI copyright issues and social media platforms' use of copyrighted film content, as well as lobbying for a federal film tax incentive.

ip_further_links.title: AI in the Patent Industry: Don't Believe the Hype. Believe the Data.
ip_further_links.summary: An IPKat analysis presents data-driven findings on the actual use and impact of AI in the patent industry, urging caution against overstated claims about AI's transformative effect on patent practice.

ip_further_links.title: Mexico's New AI Law Could Hinder USMCA Review, Warns AMITI
ip_further_links.summary: Mexico's technology industry association AMITI has warned that the country's proposed AI legislation could complicate the upcoming USMCA trade agreement review by creating regulatory conflicts with trading partners.

ip_further_links.title: Bologna Children's Book Fair 2026: AI Takes Center Stage
ip_further_links.summary: At the 2026 Bologna Children's Book Fair, AI's impact on children's publishing was a dominant theme, with discussions covering AI-generated illustrations, copyright concerns, and how publishers are adapting to new tools.

ip_further_links.title: Is the Internet's Memory at Risk? The World's Most-Used Archiving Tool Is Under Threat
ip_further_links.summary: The Wayback Machine and related internet archiving services face existential threats from legal challenges and funding pressures, raising concerns about the long-term preservation of digital knowledge.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — From Open Access to Preprints: Are We Repeating the Same Mistakes in Scholarly Publishing?
ip_further_links.summary: A guest post on The Scholarly Kitchen draws parallels between the open access movement and the rapid growth of preprints, questioning whether the academic publishing sector is repeating past policy errors.

ip_further_links.title: Bloomsbury Reorganizes Its Global Publishing Business
ip_further_links.summary: Bloomsbury Publishing has announced a reorganisation of its global publishing operations, restructuring its divisional structure as the company adapts to changing market conditions.
